page.layout: One printed page, one text column. Running head at top right, page number at top left. Margin note at left beside the second paragraph. Heading "Cap. XIIII." with its title above the text of the chapter.

main_text.p: Instrumentum autem odoratus in animantibus eodem modo differre videtur,quo molles oculi à duris.Molles enim palpebris,quasi inuolucris sepiuntur,quæ nisi aperiantur, cernere non possunt:sed eis animatibus,quæ duros habent oculos,nullę à natura datę sunt palpebræ. Eodem modo odorandi instrumentum in animantibus, quæ spiritum non ducunt,nullo velamine tectum est: iis autem quæ respirant,quoddam operculu[?]natura largita est,quod,cum ea respirant,aperitur,venis meatibusque distentis. Idcirco in aqua animantia, quæ spiritum ducunt, olfacere non possunt,quoniam respirando odorem percipiunt. Differt autem odor à sapore, quòd illę rei aridæ obiectum sit, hic vero rei humidæ.
main_text.head: CAP. XIIII. De gustatu & sapore.
main_text.p: C.10. l. 2. de anima.VOD[?] guftari potest,id quiddam tractabile est.eoque fit ut non sentiatur per externū medium. Nullo enim huiusmodi interiecto medio tactus percipit.Id autem corpus, in quo tanquam in materia est sapor, qui gustatur, humidum existit,propterea tactus quoddam obiectum est. Nihil igitur siccum mouet saporis sensum. Omne autem falsum corpus, etsi actu siccum est, potestate humidum exi-stit,eo quod facilę liquari possit vimque ha-bet

page.notes: The initial word is a woodcut initial; its first letter is read as V, probably the start of "Quod", so it is marked [?]. The word after the initial is clear. The character after "operculu" is a printer's mark or damaged type, so it is marked [?] and the word is read as "operculum". "fa-poris" is read as "sa-poris" (long s). "exi-ftit" and "ha-bet" carry printed hyphens across line ends. "Cap." heading is printed in spaced capitals; the title is in italic.
